Recover Value from Warehouse Dead Stock

Thematic Area: Inventory Recovery & Circular Commerce

How might we connect suitable warehouse dead stock with relevant buyers to recover value and release storage capacity?

Background

A shipping and logistics group wants a practical sales strategy for stock remaining in its warehouses. It needs to identify goods for sale, select suitable channels and coordinate the clearance process.

The objective is to turn authorised inventory into recoverable value while accounting for condition, pricing and fulfilment costs. Relevant partners offer liquidation channels, wholesale marketplaces, multichannel commerce software and business-to-business sales tools.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Continued storage pressure: Unsold stock occupies space needed for other warehouse activities.
  • Lower value recovery: Changing product condition and commercial relevance reduce selling opportunities over time.
  • Slower sales conversion: Fragmented listings and buyer follow-up make suitable stock harder to move into paid orders.

Existing Efforts

  • Existing group channel: The investment portfolio includes a liquidation and wholesale business, providing a starting point for inventory assessment and sales-channel selection.
  • Available capabilities: Multichannel listing, inventory and order-management tools support clearance sales. Business-to-business sales software organises reseller prospects, quotations and follow-up.
  • Collaboration focus: Establish selling authority, stock condition, quantities, minimum prices and fulfilment responsibilities. Connect inventory assessment, buyer engagement and paid orders, measuring time to sale and net value recovered.

Potential Market Size

  • US retail returns: US retail returns were projected at US$849.9 billion for 2025, illustrating the scale of goods requiring disposition and resale channels.
  • Global surplus-marketplace activity: A global surplus marketplace operator reported US$1.57 billion in transaction value in FY2025, up 15%, demonstrating established commercial activity through a single resale platform.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
